fact: Kenyans.co.ke reports ArdhiSasa is the government's digital platform for land information and land services, with an outage announced on 2026-09-21 affecting land searches, transfers, title and lease registration and other transactions.

Kenyans.co.ke reports ArdhiSasa lets users conduct land searches, property transfers, title and lease registration, stamp duty and land-rent payments without relying entirely on physical government offices.
Kenyans.co.ke reports the FAO and the Council of Governors run a digital land governance programme targeting all 47 counties to strengthen use of digital land information and geospatial technologies.
The Law Society of Kenya says Ardhisasa has become a central platform for delivery of land administration services in Kenya, with essential land services migrated to it.
The Law Society of Kenya says advocates' land searches, transfers, registrations and valuations are carried out on Ardhisasa and were disrupted by its unavailability from 2026-09-01.
Vihiga County's governor says its Land Information System is 70 percent complete, built on geospatial infrastructure.

PS Korir told the Public Accounts Committee that Ardhisasa has been rolled out in Nairobi, Murang'a, Mombasa Island and Isiolo, while the Auditor-General found only Nairobi and Murang'a fully migrated of 83 registries.
Kenya News Agency reports Ardhisasa digital land records are operational in Nairobi and Murang'a, where 387,635 registers and 269,694 files were scanned since 2021 and uploaded to the platform.
Kenya News Agency quotes the Lands Cabinet Secretary saying residents can open Ardhisasa accounts to transact on their land digitally and get alerts of any attempted transaction.

FAO Kenya reports the EU- and FAO-co-financed Digital Land Governance Programme is sorting, barcoding and scanning land records in 10 registries in Kajiado, Baringo and Machakos counties as part of ongoing digitisation.

Capital FM reports the national land records digitisation programme, converting physical records to digital form, covered Nairobi and Murang'a in its first phase and will extend to fifteen more counties.
Kenya's State Department for Lands says Ardhisasa, its National Land Information Management System, is live in Nairobi, Murang'a and Mombasa, while many land offices still rely on manual processes.
GIM International reported in 2025 that Kenya's digital land system Ardhisasa is operational in two counties since 2021 while land files and cadastral maps are still being digitised.
